name: Self-limited Childhood Occipital Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Self-limited Childhood Occipital Epilepsy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of focal seizures with visual symptoms such as elementary visual hallucinations or blindness
Onset of seizures typically between ages 3 and 15 years
Ictal or interictal EEG showing occipital epileptiform discharges
Normal neurodevelopment and neurological examination between seizures
Spontaneous remission of seizures within a few years without neurological sequelae

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical focal visual seizures with occipital EEG abnormalities and onset between 3 and 15 years
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by EEG; neuroimaging is typically normal.

pathognomonic.symptomName: EEG with occipital focal spike waves
searchTerms: EEG showing spikes in back of brain
brain wave spikes in occipital area
preference to look in one direction

genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; familial cases reported
other: EEG with occipital spikes or sharp waves during or between seizures

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly autonomic seizures with vomiting and pallor
EEG shows occipital spikes but clinical presentation differs
Typical absence seizures with generalized 3 Hz spike-and-wave on EEG

redFlags: Seizure onset before age 3 or after age 15
references: Panayiotopoulos CP. A clinical guide to epileptic syndromes and their treatment. Springer; 2010.
Orphanet: Self-limited childhood occipital epilepsy. ORPHA:25968.

Berg AT, et al. Revised terminology and concepts for organization of seizures and epilepsies: report of the ILAE Commission on Classification and Terminology, 2005-2009. Epilepsia. 2010 Apr;51(4):676-85.
